AudioAssetStimulus.description:
A listening recording. Each listening section may carry its OWN track.

Per-part audio (Cambridge YLE ships one mp3 per part): consecutive listening
sections form one *track* while their `asset_id` stays the same; a section whose
`asset_id` differs from the previous audio section's starts a NEW track, and a
listening section with a non-audio stimulus (e.g. a matching pool) continues the
current one. The track's settings (`plays`, `locked`, `preview_asset_id`) come
from the section that starts it. Tracks play strictly in order (the runner never
lets a later part's track start before the current one has ended); the
furthest position per track (`asset_id`) is stored server-side
(`AudioTrackProgress`). One `asset_id` may only be used by consecutive sections
(the editor refuses A, B, A).

images.description: Optional context image asset_ids shown beside this stimulus.
images.title: Images

locked.description: When true the main track cannot be paused, seeked, or replayed once started (leaving/answering does not stop it); the preview clip stays free.
locked.title: Locked

plays.description: Replay limit for the main track. Default 1: Cambridge recordings already bake in the double play, so the online track is played once start-to-end.
plays.title: Plays

preview_asset_id.description: Optional sound-check / instructions clip (the recording's opening explanation), played BEFORE the main track and freely replayable.
preview_asset_id.title: Preview Asset Id

AudioAssetStimulus.title: AudioAssetStimulus

ColourTaskItem.description:
A 'listen and colour' task (YLE). The student paints a line-art scene; it is
teacher-reviewed (never auto-scored), like writing. The colouring `key` is
authoring-only guidance and, like `rubric`, never reaches the student.

key.description: What to colour what — teacher review guidance (never served).
key.title: Key

palette.description: Selectable brush colours offered to the student.
palette.title: Palette

points.description: Marks this item is worth (1-20). None = default (objective 1, writing / colouring 5). Objective: a right answer earns all of them. Writing: the grader's 0-5 band is scaled to it. Authoring-only, never served.
points.title: Points

ColourTaskItem.title: ColourTaskItem

DrawingItem.description:
A free-hand drawing on a canvas over a picture (IQ "draw what is missing",
"divide the square"). Graded deterministically by `app/grading/drawing.py`;
a low-confidence verdict goes to the teacher's review queue (`needs_review`).

Response: a JSON string {"w": W, "h": H, "strokes": [[[x, y], ...], ...]} in
canvas pixels (the canvas covers the picture). `target` is authoring-only.

asset_id.description: The picture shown under the canvas.
asset_id.title: Asset Id

points.description: Marks this item is worth (1-20). None = default (objective 1, writing / colouring 5). Objective: a right answer earns all of them. Writing: the grader's 0-5 band is scaled to it. Authoring-only, never served.
points.title: Points

DrawingItem.title: DrawingItem

DrawingLinesTarget.description:
"Divide the square": the student's strokes must reproduce `segments`.

Segments are in square-local coordinates ((0,0) = the square's top-left,
(1,1) = its bottom-right). `tolerance` is a distance in square sides. With
`allow_transforms` the answer may be rotated 90/180/270 or mirrored (the 8
symmetries of the square). Ink ON the square's border is ignored when
`ignore_border` (the border is printed). Authoring-only (except `square`,
which the client twin carries).
DrawingLinesTarget.title: DrawingLinesTarget

DrawingRegionTarget.description:
"Draw what is missing": the ink must fall (mostly) inside the zones.

Ink length is measured in PICTURE WIDTHS (1.0 = a stroke as long as the picture
is wide). Correct when total ink >= `min_ink`, ink inside the zones (dilated by
`margin`) / total ink >= `min_inside_ratio`, and — with `require_all_zones` —
every zone holds at least `min_ink / len(zones)` of ink. Authoring-only.
DrawingRegionTarget.title: DrawingRegionTarget

image.description: Optional picture shown with the gap (asset_id), e.g. the symbol whose number the student recalls. Must exist in storage on import.
image.title: Image

max_words.description: Most words the answer may have (open cloze / word formation = 1). A longer answer, or two answers given, is wrong: a '/', a backslash or '|' in the response ('in/on') counts as two answers. Words are split on whitespace ('7.30' is one word); contractions count as two words (B2: except can't). An answer equal to an accepted key is never failed by this rule. Shown to the student. None = no limit.
max_words.title: Max Words

numeric.description: The answer is a number: the runner opens the numeric keyboard (inputmode=numeric). A display hint only — grading is unchanged.
numeric.title: Numeric

points.description: Marks this item is worth (1-20). None = default (objective 1, writing / colouring 5). Objective: a right answer earns all of them. Writing: the grader's 0-5 band is scaled to it. Authoring-only, never served.
points.title: Points

rejected.description: Forms the key marks WRONG although they are close to an accepted answer (a different word form / common grammar error, e.g. 'goes' for 'go'). Never typo-accepted. Authoring-only, never served.
rejected.title: Rejected

spelling.description: Spelling policy for grading. 'exact' = only the listed answers count; 'tolerant' = recognisable misspellings are accepted. None = derive from the section skill: reading / writing -> exact (open cloze), listening -> tolerant (set 'exact' for a word spelled out letter by letter); C1 / C2 listening and Use of English -> exact. Authoring-only, never served.
spelling.title: Spelling

stem_word.description: Word formation (B2-C2 Use of English Part 3): the stem the answer is derived from, shown to the student beside the gap, e.g. 'COMPETE'.
stem_word.title: Stem Word

images.title: Images

text.description: Passage text with gap markers (PET Reading Part 4).
text.title: Text

IntroPractice.description:
A booklet PRACTICE problem done on the intro's Example screen, before the
clock: the student answers, presses Check and sees right / wrong + the printed
answer.

NOT a scored item: never graded, never saved as an answer, never counted. Its
`solution` is PUBLIC by design — the booklet prints it next to the practice —
so it is served with the intro. Golden rule #1 is about scored items: their
keys still never reach the client (`tests/test_no_correct_invariant.py` checks
that `solution` exists only here, under `SectionIntro.practice`).

kinds: `text` = type the answer (checked case-insensitively, spaces collapsed);
`choice` = pick one of `options` (`solution` = its key); `mark` = mark the row
or not (`solution` "1" / "0"); `drawing` = a not-checked "try it" canvas over
`images[0]` with a "show answer" (`solution_images` and/or `explanation`).

images.description: Optional context image asset_ids shown beside this stimulus.
images.title: Images

solution.description: The printed (public) answer of this practice problem — see the class doc; scored items never carry one.
solution.title: Solution

solution_images.description: Pictures of the printed answer (asset ids).
solution_images.title: Solution Images

IntroPractice.title: IntroPractice

KeyWordTransformationItem.description:
Key word transformation (B2-C2 Use of English Part 4).

The student reads the lead-in sentence (`prompt`), sees the KEY WORD and
completes the second sentence (`gapped_sentence`, one gap) in `min_words` ..
`max_words` words INCLUDING the unchanged key word. Marked per half (0, 1 or 2;
`points` defaults to 2). Authoring-only key: `answers`.

gapped_sentence.description: The second sentence with exactly ONE gap marker (`____`).
gapped_sentence.title: Gapped Sentence

points.description: Marks this item is worth (1-20). None = default (objective 1, writing / colouring 5). Objective: a right answer earns all of them. Writing: the grader's 0-5 band is scaled to it. Authoring-only, never served.
points.title: Points

prompt.description: The lead-in sentence the student transforms.
prompt.title: Prompt

KeyWordTransformationItem.title: KeyWordTransformationItem

KwtAnswer.description:
One acceptable answer pattern of a key word transformation, split in two.

Each half is worth one mark (Cambridge: "The mark scheme splits the answer into
two parts and candidates gain one mark for each part which is correct"). Each
half lists its own acceptable texts (`are said` / `is said`); the key's
`a | b OR c | d` becomes two `KwtAnswer`s, and alternatives may split at
different points (`may have | forgotten` OR `may | have forgotten`).

part_a.description: Acceptable texts of the FIRST half (1 mark).
part_a.title: Part A

part_b.description: Acceptable texts of the SECOND half (1 mark).
part_b.title: Part B

KwtAnswer.title: KwtAnswer

MarkToggleItem.description:
One row the student may mark or leave unmarked (e.g. "put an X on every pair
that is NOT identical"). Response: "1" = marked, "0" / "" / none = unmarked.

Graded PER SECTION (`app/grading/mark_toggle.py`): a row with `correct=True`
is worth 1 point when marked; a `correct=False` row is worth 0, but each FALSE
mark cancels one correct mark of the same section (floor 0) — marking every
row earns nothing. `correct` is authoring-only, never served.

correct.description: True = this row SHOULD be marked (authoring-only).
correct.title: Correct

correct.description: `key` of the correct option in the section pool.
correct.title: Correct

audio.description: The recording a LISTENING matching part plays (C1/C2 Listening Part 4: two parallel tasks, each with its own A-H pool, over one recording). It opens / continues a listening track exactly like an `audio_asset` stimulus: consecutive sections with the same `audio.asset_id` share ONE track (played once for both tasks). None = the part continues the current track.

each_option_once.description: True = every option fits at most ONE question (a gapped text: B2 Reading Part 6, C1 Part 7, C2 Part 6 - one option is a distractor); the runner greys out an option already used in this part. False = options are reusable (multiple matching: 'some options may be correct for more than one question'). Display hint only - grading compares each item's key.
each_option_once.title: Each Option Once

SectionStudy.description:
A show-then-hide stimulus (memory subtests): shown for `study_seconds`, then
removed before the recall items appear. A picture (`asset_id`) and/or `text`.

Authoring model. NEVER part of the bulk `ClientSection`: the section only says
that a study phase exists (`ClientStudyInfo`); the content travels as a separate
`ClientStudyStimulus`, which delivery serves only inside the study window (see
app/delivery/CLAUDE.md "Study stimulus contract").
SectionStudy.title: SectionStudy
